Design a short survey that would actually settle this objective. Between 5 and 8 questions.
Prefer multiple choice and rating scales over free text, because you must analyse the answers
yourself afterwards. Include at least one open question so you can learn something you did
not think to ask about. Do not ask for names or contact details.

}

args.brief:
Create a survey titled "Columbia AI Club — Spring Event Planning Survey".
It exists to answer this objective: Figure out the best event to put on for the Columbia AI Club next spring

Use exactly these questions, in this order:
1. [single] Which of the following best describes your current involvement with AI? Options: I take AI/ML courses but don't work on projects outside class / I work on personal or research AI projects / I'm actively job-seeking or interning in AI/ML / I'm mostly curious — I follow AI news but haven't built anything yet / I'm not very involved with AI right now.
2. [single] Which event format would you most want the Columbia AI Club to host this spring? (Pick one) Options: Hands-on workshop (learn a tool or technique by building something) / Hackathon (multi-hour or overnight project competition) / Speaker / panel (industry or research guests) / Networking mixer (meet peers, researchers, and recruiters) / Paper reading / research discussion group / Demo day (students showcase their own AI projects).
3. [multi] Which AI topics are you most excited to explore? (Select up to 3) Options: Large language models and generative AI / Computer vision / Reinforcement learning and agents / AI for social good / ethics and policy / AI in healthcare or science / Robotics / AI product / startup / entrepreneurship / ML engineering and deployment (MLOps).
4. [scale] How likely are you to attend a Columbia AI Club event this spring? Options: 1 — Very unlikely / 2 / 3 / 4 / 5 — Very likely.
5. [single] What time commitment works best for you for a single event? Options: Under 1 hour / 1–2 hours / Half a day (3–4 hours) / Full day (6–8 hours) / Multi-day (e.g., overnight hackathon).
6. [single] What is the single most important thing an AI Club event could give you? Options: Practical skills I can put on a résumé / Connections with recruiters or companies / Connections with other students working on AI / Exposure to cutting-edge research / A finished project or portfolio piece / Just a fun, low-pressure experience.
7. [open] Is there anything you wish the Columbia AI Club would do that it hasn't done yet — or anything that would make you much more likely to come to an event?

Keep it short and plain. Do not add demographic questions I have not asked for.
Publish it as soon as it is ready.
